correctness.rationale: Exact combinatorial product face lattice follows by crossing original simplex faces on both sign sides. Proper Crofton normalization requires the directional-width-biased normal, and independent Gaussian radius cancels from expected gaps. Edge summation gives \(\mathbb E f_0(n)=n(n-1)/(2\sqrt\pi\,\mathbb E M_n)\). For asymptotics, normalized Gaussian maxima/minima tend to \(\pm1\), the Crofton tilt tends to one in \(L^1\) (nonnegative density, unit mean and convergence in probability), and binomial Gaussian-tail bracketing proves smaller-side count exponent \(1-U^2\); product-face estimates yield all fixed ranks jointly. Nonstandard change of measure and finite normalizations were independently re-derived and tested with 140000 weighted Gaussian samples per small dimension, full crossed-face enumeration, and larger-dimensional experiments. Simulations are corroboration, not proof.

originality.rationale: The full finite face-vector law under invariant *affine* hyperplanes and the joint nonconstant limit of logarithmic face counts are not stated or implied by the inspected closest primary results. The 2023 chamber theorem identifies changes in crossing-edge sets but does not integrate the invariant measure or derive Gaussian-gap weights or the uniform-square exponent. The 2020 non-central section work optimizes volume/perimeter. Published central-section fluctuation findings fix offset at the centroid and have a different probability space. Linear Crofton integration and the known Gaussian maximum formula may give the vertex mean, but do not imply the distribution or its typical exponent. Historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: For the fundamental regular simplex, the entire invariant-affine-section face-vector probability law is specified at finite \(n\), plus a continuum-valued typical growth exponent and an asymptotic expectation exhibiting strong mean-versus-typical separation. These structural results quantify kinematic section complexity across dimension, beyond individual Crofton expectations or generic chamber classification; the precise invariant sampling law is essential to the question. The fixed-rank joint limit informs multiple canonical geometric invariants in one theorem.
